defects: (a) SCRATCH FILES OUTSIDE THE SCRATCHPAD, BEFORE THE SEAL. A byte comparison of the seven companions against their deposited bytes wrote two scratch files under the shell's /tmp and not the session's scratchpad; they were removed in the same command, each path verified with test -e before its rm. Nothing else was touched; nothing was tracked or staged. Declared on the face, section (0).

(b) A DELETE VERIFIED IN ONE FORM AND MADE IN ANOTHER, BEFORE THE SEAL. A dry report call of the step-zero runner wrote data/b639_tests_stepzero.txt with no test run; the command that removed it verified the path in relative form and removed it in absolute form -- the same file, the house delete form (b537, standing) not followed to the letter. The bank was rewritten by the runner's report after every test ran. Declared on the face, section (0).

(c) THE LOCK CALLED WITHOUT ITS DIRECTORY. The first reg_seal --lock named the face without data/ and was refused with nothing written (the b633 trap); the lock was written by the second call on the full path, the seal verified intact.

(d) THE PROMPT PUT BEFORE ITS FIGURE WAS READ TO THE AUTHOR. The deposit prompt was first put beside a summary of H73b; the author returned it unanswered to read the description first, the bank was printed whole, and the prompt was put again and answered hold. The answers bank carries both calls as the transcript holds them, the first with no answer, and the sealed G-ANSWERS-BANKED reads that unanswered prompt in its letter.

(e) A SEALED ARM THAT CANNOT PASS. G-FILES-BANK reads a file's kind by the first word of its label, and the label INHERITED, BYTE-IDENTICAL reads as INHERITED with its comma, so its count of nine replaced, two inherited and three added can never match; its other clauses hold, every one of the fourteen sha256 values re-read equal to the bank and the inherited md5s v1.1.2's (relay data/b639_checks.txt). The predicate was the seat's, written before the seal and not run against a written file bank there; it is refuted in its letter and left unedited.
